traits.stem_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Opuntia basilaris: 'Stem segments ... blue- to yellow-green, sometimes tinged maroon-purple ... papillose to puberulent'; Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 490: 'blue-green, often tinged purple'. A puberulent pad's blue-green reads grey in the sun; with no shade named it was measured: the median of the pixels inside sunlit pads of seven iNaturalist photographs (imagekit batch inat-cacti-2026-10-19, photos 0, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10 in key order), the brighter three quarters of each, then the median of the photos: RGB 146, 146, 128, a grey-green (the purple-tinged pads of photo 10 read 109, 90, 87). Until 2026-10-19 a lavender blue, RGB 115, 120, 140, read from Anderson's words.

traits.flower_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 490, Opuntia basilaris: flowers cherry red to yellow, rarely white (cherry red here, as usual), 5 to 7.5 cm long and across; fruit green, dry when ripe, spineless, 2.5 to 3 cm long (a dull dry green here).

traits.flower_size_m.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 490, Opuntia basilaris: flowers cherry red to yellow, rarely white (cherry red here, as usual), 5 to 7.5 cm long and across; fruit green, dry when ripe, spineless, 2.5 to 3 cm long (a dull dry green here).

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Opuntia basilaris: fruits maturing tan, 20 to 40 by 15 to 23 mm, dry at maturity, puberulent, spineless. Until 2026-10-18 a dull dry green from Anderson (2001) p. 490, 'fruit green, dry when ripe'.

traits.glochid_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Opuntia basilaris: glochids numerous, nearly filling the areoles, yellow to red-brown or dark brown, to 3 mm; a red-brown here, as Britton and Rose's 'glochids brownish' (1919, p. 120).

traits.areole_wool_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Opuntia basilaris: areoles circular to elliptic, 3 to 5 by 3 mm; wool white to tan, ageing grey; a pale tan here.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 490, Opuntia basilaris: flowers cherry red to yellow, rarely white (cherry red here, as usual), 5 to 7.5 cm long and across; fruit green, dry when ripe, spineless, 2.5 to 3 cm long (a dull dry green here).

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 490, Opuntia basilaris: fruit 2.5 to 3 cm long and 1.5 to 2.2 cm in diameter.

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, p. 120): joints broadly obovate, 8 to 20 cm long; spines none, or rarely a few on the upper areoles; glochids brownish.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a low clump under 40 cm tall of pads 5 to 20 cm long, fanning out from the base. Bright magenta flowers along the top of the pads in spring. Not fitted to measurements. Pads stand two generations deep, not three, after FNA vol. 4 (eFloras, Opuntia basilaris): "forming clumps, 1-2(-3) segments tall, to 7-40 cm" (2026-10-18).

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: 20 to 40 cm. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: blue-grey pads, often purple-tinged, with no long spines; the sunken areoles carry dense tufts of reddish-brown glochids. Its flower, bud and fruit are drawn from its characters by the rules at Cactaceae and the flowering plants: tepals on a spiral, as many and as broad as the family's rules give, on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, its stamens, style and stigma lobes, and its fruit from its stated colour, size and surface. Until 2026-10-18 its flower and fruit looks were partly set by hand (round tepal tips, a centre and an accent colour by eye), and a look set by hand keeps the rule that gives it the year its months state from running, so it flowered and fruited all year.

Until 2026-10-18 a model estimate of June to August.
